subject: Order Form / SLA redline coordination - maintenance windows & credits
messages:
From: Aisha Thomas <aisha.thomas@lumenflow.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@lumenflow.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA redlines from procurement (order form + maintenance windows)

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — LumenFlow's procurement team has gone through the MSA + order form and sent back SLA redlines. The key asks are: tighter uptime commitment during business hours, clearer escalation windows for P1/P2, and a higher cap on service credits for prolonged incidents.

I attached the redlines (LumenFlow_SLA_redlines_v1.docx) and a small packet showing our expected traffic profile (evidence_packet_svc_metrics.csv). Our legal and SRE teams are aligned on these priorities and want to get to a mutually acceptable order form this month.

Can you confirm who on your side will own the SLA counterproposal and whether Redwood can accept a 99.95% target for the primary region with a scaled credit matrix? Also need clarity on allowed maintenance windows — we want to avoid rolling maintenance during our peak window (Mon–Fri 09:00–18:00 PT).

Appreciate a quick alignment call if helpful.

Best,
Aisha Thomas
Head of Procurement, LumenFlow Inc.
A: +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: LumenFlow_SLA_redlines_v1.docx; evidence_packet_svc_metrics.csv

Subject: Re: SLA redlines from procurement (order form + maintenance windows)

Hi Aisha — thanks for sending these over and for the packet, that was helpful. Quick answers up front:
- Primary owner for the counterproposal will be me (Ben) working with Legal (Laura) and Ops (Rachel).
- We can take a 99.95% uptime target for the primary region as a starting point but need to sync on the credit ladder and the measurement window.
- Regarding maintenance: we generally schedule non-emergency rolling maintenance in the 02:00–06:00 PT window and avoid peak hours. We can formalize a blackout window for 09:00–18:00 PT on Mon–Fri for your account if that aligns with capacity planning.

I looped in Rachel (technical account lead) and Laura (legal) to propose a redline response. Laura, Rachel — can you review the attached doc and confirm any non-starters? I’ll propose an internal markup and then push a counter to Aisha & Marco within 48hrs.

Call cadence: does Thurs 13 May 10:00 PT work for a short alignment?

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: review LumenFlow SLA redlines

Ben / Rachel — read through Aisha's redlines. Summary of our position and recommended edits:

1) Uptime target: 99.95% is acceptable for the primary region if we limit applicability to production endpoints explicitly enumerated in the order form. We should push back on any language that broadens the metric to dev/test or multi-region aggregates.

2) Measurement window: recommend we keep a trailing 30-day measurement, not calendar-month, to avoid gaming and to match our monitoring pipeline. If they insist on calendar-month, require a mutually agreed measurement playbook (logs and source of truth).

3) Credits cap: we can accept a graduated credit ladder but need to cap at 50% of monthly spend per incident and 150% aggregate per rolling 12 months. Anything above needs executive sign-off.

4) Emergency maintenance carveout: propose adding a clause that requires 24hrs notice where practicable and a maximum of 6 emergency maintenance events per 12-month period before we agree to an operational review.

5) Response times: P1 (platform down) — 1 hour initial response, P2 (degraded) — 4 hours, on-call escalation matrix attached. We should not accept a 15-minute paging SLA for all incidents.

I made inline comments in the attached doc (redlines). Rachel please confirm whether the 02:00–06:00 PT maintenance window is sufficient and whether our runbook can guarantee no impact during LumenFlow peak hours if blackout windows are enforced.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA redlines from procurement (order form + maintenance windows)

Aisha / Ben / Laura — quick ops note after looking at their traffic sample:

- Peak is concentrated 10:00–16:00 PT Mon–Fri; we can enforce a hard blackout for that window for standard maintenance. For critical security patches we would need a documented emergency process but will provide 24hr notice where possible.
- The 99.95% baseline is OK, however that equates to ~21.6 minutes/mo downtime. We should call that out in the counter so LumenFlow understands the math and the credit triggers.
- On runbook: I can attach a runbook excerpt showing monitoring sources and incident timeline expectations — that should address their request for measurable evidence.

Proposed next steps:
1) Ben to send a written counter with Laura's legal language and Ops-runbook excerpt.
2) If they accept, we’ll prepare a redlined order form and DocuSign envelope.
3) If they push credit caps higher, route to sales leadership for approval.

Rachel Kim
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0178

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Thomas <aisha.thomas@lumenflow.com>, Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@lumenflow.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood counterproposal — SLA + maintenance window wording

Hi Aisha / Marco — thanks for your patience. Attached is our consolidated counter (we included Laura's and Rachel's points). High-level bullets below; full redline attached.

- Uptime: Redwood proposes 99.95% uptime for the Production endpoints enumerated in the order form. Measurement: rolling 30-day window (source: Redwood monitoring pipeline).
- Credits: graduated ladder (4 tiers) with a per-incident cap of 50% of monthly fees and aggregate cap of 150% per rolling 12 months. Executive review required above that.
- Response times: P1 initial response within 1 hour, P2 within 4 hours. Detailed escalation ladder included.
- Maintenance: standard maintenance restricted to 02:00–06:00 PT. We will institute a blackout window 09:00–18:00 PT Mon–Fri for your account; any maintenance outside that requires written agreement. Emergency maintenance carveouts require 24hr notice where practicable; we will limit emergency events and include a remediation review if they breach thresholds.

We can take this to DocuSign once you confirm the attached counter is acceptable. I’ve also added a short ops excerpt to show monitoring/evidence sources. If anything in the legal redline is a non-starter, flag the exact clause so Laura and I can escalate.

Proposed next step: confirm by Tue 18 May so we can finalize before the end of the month.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_SLA_counter_v2.docx; ops_runbook_excerpt.pdf

Ben / team — thanks for the clear counter. We reviewed internally and have two follow-ups before we can sign: 1) request clarification on the calculation methodology for the 30-day rolling window (need exact metric name + primary aggregation source), and 2) propose changing the aggregate annual cap from 150% to 200% for the first 12 months while we ramp.

We can live with the blackout window and the response ladders — nice to see the ops excerpt. For transparency I'll ask Marco (SRE) to join a short call to validate the monitoring source on Tue 18 May 10:00 PT. If you can share the exact metric/ID ahead of the call and drop a DocuSign envelope with the counter while we discuss the aggregate cap, that would speed things up.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Aisha
